chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us in the year 273 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the year 229 AH, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that one of his companions entered upon him.

He said to him: 'May I be your ransom, by Allah I love you and love whoever loves you. O my master, how many your Shia are!' He said to him: 'Mention them.' He said: 'They are many.' He said: 'Can you count them?' He said: 'They are more than that.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'If the specified number were completed at three hundred and eleven, that would be what you want. But our Shia are those whose voice does not exceed their hearing, nor their zeal their body; nor do they praise us openly, nor quarrel with us publicly, nor sit with us criticizing, nor talk with us abusing, nor love whoever hates us, nor hate whoever loves us.'

I said: 'Then what should I do with these differing Shia groups who claim they are Shia?' He said: 'Among them is distinction, among them is purification, and among them is alteration. Years will come that will perish them, a sword that will kill them, and disagreement that will scatter them. Our true Shia are those who do not growl like a dog, nor covet like a crow, nor ask people with their hand even if they die of hunger.'

I said: 'May I be your ransom, where should I seek these described with this description?' He said: 'Seek them in the far corners of the earth. Those are they whose livelihood is humble, whose dwelling is transient. If they are present, they are not recognized; if absent, they are not missed; if sick, they are not visited; if proposed to, they are not married; if they die, they are not attended. Those are they who share their wealth among themselves, and visit each other in their graves, and their desires do not differ even if the lands differ. If they see a believer, they honor him; if they see a hypocrite, they leave him. At death they do not despair, and in their graves they visit each other…'

key_terms.الهَرِير: The growling sound of a dog
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ الْمَوْصُوفَةُ: The specified number (referring to a prophesied count)

ai.seo_question: What are the distinguishing characteristics of the true Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the 'true Shia' not by numerical majority but by the virtues of humility, secrecy, and self-sufficiency, contrasting them with the fragmented false groups who will be eliminated by time, war, and doctrinal divergence. This narration is pivotal in Shia eschatology, offering reassurance during the Minor and Major Ghebah that the faithful, though geographically dispersed and socially invisible, remain spiritually united and distinct from the masses.
